lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Exploring Europe
lesson.summary: Locate European countries and compare their landscapes, climates and cities.
learning_objectives: Locate countries and cities on a map of Europe
Explain how climate differs across Europe

standards.text: Name and locate countries and cities of Europe; describe physical and human features; understand climate patterns

success_criteria: I can find countries and capitals on a map of Europe
I can describe physical and human features
I can explain why climates differ
lesson.real_life: The UK is part of Europe, many Pakistani-British families travel in Europe, and Muslim heritage can be seen in Cordoba in Spain and in Sarajevo.

warm_up.explanation: The Atlantic lies to the west.

warm_up.prompt: The Alps are a mountain range.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how diverse is Europe?
blocks.say: Today we explore Europe. How do its landscapes, climates and cities differ from place to place?

blocks.alt: Snow-capped mountains above a green valley with a small village and forested slopes under a blue sky
blocks.caption: A valley in the Alps, with snow on the high peaks.
blocks.credit: Photo by Christopher Politano on Unsplash
blocks.say: This valley lies in the Alps, a great mountain range that crosses several European countries.

blocks.markdown: A **continent** is one of the seven great land areas of the Earth.
blocks.say: Europe is a continent in the north-west of the Eurasian landmass. It has more than forty countries.

blocks.markdown: A **country** is smaller than a continent.
blocks.say: It is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean in the west and the Mediterranean Sea in the south.

scenes.caption: A continent.
scenes.say: Europe is a continent. It has many countries, such as France and Italy.

scenes.caption: Seas.
scenes.say: The Atlantic Ocean lies to the west. The Mediterranean Sea lies to the south.

scenes.caption: Mountains.
scenes.say: The Alps, the Pyrenees and other mountain ranges cross the continent.

question.explanation: Europe is a continent with many countries.

options.text: A continent made up of many countries

blocks.alt: Rooftops and a domed church in Rome at sunset with warm-coloured buildings and a blue sky
blocks.caption: Rooftops and domes in Rome, the capital of Italy.
blocks.credit: Photo by Francesco Maria Achille on Unsplash
blocks.say: Every country has a capital city. Rome is the capital of Italy and Paris is the capital of France.

blocks.markdown: A **capital city** is where a country's government sits.
blocks.say: Capital cities are where governments meet. Many are also big centres of culture and trade.

scenes.caption: London and Paris.
scenes.say: London is the capital of the UK. Paris is the capital of France.

scenes.caption: Rome and Madrid.
scenes.say: Rome is the capital of Italy. Madrid is the capital of Spain.

scenes.caption: Berlin.
scenes.say: Berlin is the capital of Germany. Not every capital is on the coast.

question.prompt: Rome is the capital of Italy.

blocks.title: Hina plans a trip to Italy
blocks.transcript: Hina looks at a map of Europe in her home in Manchester. Her family wants to visit northern Italy. Rome is the capital. On the way, they will cross the Alps. Scotland is wet because Atlantic winds bring a lot of rain. Italy has a Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers. She packs light clothes, a sun hat and walking shoes. She plans to respect local customs and keep places clean. Hina writes a postcard home about Europe's many landscapes.
blocks.caption: Hina plans a family trip from Manchester to northern Italy and learns why Italy is warm and Scotland is wet.

blocks.say: Europe has high mountains, long rivers and wide plains. These are its physical features.

blocks.markdown: A **river** carries water across land to the sea.
blocks.say: The Alps include Mont Blanc, about 4,800 metres high. The Danube flows through many countries.

scenes.caption: The Alps.
scenes.say: The Alps stretch across France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria and more.

scenes.caption: The Danube.
scenes.say: The Danube starts in Germany and flows east to the Black Sea.

scenes.caption: Rivers.
scenes.say: Rivers like the Thames and the Rhine carry trade and give water.

blocks.caption: A village on the Mediterranean coast of Italy, with a small harbour.
blocks.credit: Photo by Josh Hild on Unsplash
blocks.say: Europe has a long, winding coastline. Many towns grew up by the sea, as in Italy.

blocks.markdown: A **plain** is a large, flat area of land.
blocks.say: Wide plains stretch across the east and north. These are good for farming.

scenes.caption: Coast.
scenes.say: The Mediterranean coast has warm seas, beaches and old harbours.

scenes.caption: Plains.

scenes.caption: Ports.

blocks.markdown: **Climate** is the usual weather over many years.
blocks.say: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years. Europe has several climates.

scenes.caption: Mediterranean.
scenes.say: The Mediterranean climate has hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters.

scenes.caption: Atlantic.
scenes.say: The Atlantic climate in the west is mild and wet all year.

scenes.caption: The east.
scenes.say: In the east, winters are colder and summers are warmer.

question.prompt: What is the Mediterranean climate like?

options.text: Hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters

blocks.text: Stop 2: Why the west is wetter

blocks.markdown: The Atlantic brings wet weather to the west.
blocks.say: Warm, wet winds blow in from the Atlantic. They bring rain to the west of Europe.

blocks.title: Climate clues
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Warm water called the North Atlantic Drift also keeps the west milder in winter. Warm up your memory.

scenes.caption: Winds.
scenes.say: Winds blow from the Atlantic across the land.

scenes.caption: Mountains.
scenes.say: Mountains force the air upwards. It cools and drops rain.

scenes.caption: The east.
scenes.say: By the time the air reaches the east, it holds less water.

question.explanation: Wet winds from the Atlantic reach the west first.

points: Climate is the usual weather over years

blocks.say: Let us remember. Europe has different climates. The Atlantic makes the west wet, and the south has hot, dry summers.

blocks.say: Tourism is when people travel to enjoy places. Europe is one of the most visited continents.

scenes.caption: Visitors.
scenes.say: Tourists come to see old cities, mountains and beaches.

scenes.caption: Benefits.
scenes.say: Tourism brings jobs and money to hotels, shops and guides.

scenes.caption: Problems.
scenes.say: But too many tourists can cause crowds, litter and damage.

question.prompt: Which is a benefit of tourism?

blocks.text: Stop 2: Choose a country and say why

blocks.markdown: A good plan thinks about weather, people and respect.
blocks.say: Hina plans a trip. She chooses a country, a season and a plan that respects local customs.

blocks.markdown: Muslim heritage is found across Europe.
blocks.say: For halal travel, check menus and look for halal food. Spain and Bosnia have mosques with a long history.

scenes.caption: Choose.
scenes.say: Pick a country and a season. Italy in late spring is warm and not too crowded.

scenes.caption: Pack.
scenes.say: Pack for the weather. Take light clothes, a hat and walking shoes.

scenes.caption: Respect.
scenes.say: Respect local customs. Ask before you take photos, and keep places clean.
